releases.title: Kelvaroq v0.2.0
releases.summary:
This first public launcher release opens directly to the Kelvaroq workspace. Extract the entire Windows x64 ZIP, open Kelvaroq.exe, and select the executable declared in your installation’s MicrosoftGame.Config. You can also drop the installation folder onto the workspace.

Kelvaroq is developed by Stellarr Studio SAS with Moon AI (https://realmoon.ai).

In the launcher

  • The workspace remembers your installation and shows whether shader preload and the live monitor are enabled. Preload prepares cached pipelines before launch. You can skip the remaining work.
  • The live monitor shows frame times, estimated GPU use and engine activity. Select a frame to inspect it or export recent samples to CSV. Enable the monitor in Settings.
  • Save history takes a snapshot before launch and after a clean exit. You can name a manual snapshot, restore a previous one, or export and import a ZIP. Import and restore verify file checksums and save a recovery copy first.
  • Settings lets you move the cache and title data, choose how many snapshots to keep, and select English, French, Spanish, German, Italian or Brazilian Portuguese.
  • At startup the launcher can check GitHub for a newer public release. When one is available, a notice shows the version, a short excerpt from the notes, and a link to the release page. Settings and About also offer a manual check. All checks share a 24-hour limit. You can turn them off in Settings and use the workspace offline.

Set VICTORY_LAUNCHER_V2=0 to use the original picker. The packaged engine is native/kelvaroq-engine.exe.

The workspace now shows the detected GPU, dedicated video memory, CPU and system memory. It reports missing graphics features before launch. Settings opens in Automatic mode and shows the memory budgets and worker count selected for this PC. Custom mode saves overrides for the next launch. An inherited environment value takes precedence in either mode.

Measured performance

In a 300-second warm-cache run on an RTX 5080, heavy frames had a median of 108.5 ms, a 95th percentile of 261.5 ms, and a mean of 132.2 ms (7.6 fps). GPU busy time was about 30%. An external 36-minute session at 2560 × 1440 on a Ryzen 9 7950X, RTX 4090 and 32 GB RAM averaged 10 fps overall and 10.9 fps after loading. These measurements cover different workloads. The 30 fps target corresponds to 33.3 ms per frame. Measurement details

Requirements and credits

Use 64-bit Windows, .NET Framework 4.8 for the desktop workspace, a Direct3D 12-capable GPU and driver, and a legally obtained local installation. Keep the extracted files together. The ZIP includes the native runtime, the reference interpreter and dependency notices.

The native engine derives from VIctory and victory-fork, both GPL-3.0-or-later. The package includes their licence in notices/native/LICENSE, the build record in native/build.json, and the corresponding source in sources/native.zip.

releases.title: v2026.11.27.7
releases.summary:
Fixes for "the newest version doesn't launch". Put victory.exe beside game_scarlett_master.exe and double-click it, as before.

VILauncher: "Fix and verify" said no Agility SDK package holds the project's files

VILauncher reads the repository to learn which D3D12Core.dll this fork expects. Our download script listed the package's SHA-256 before the DLL's, so the launcher took the package's hash as the DLL's and refused every Microsoft package ("No Microsoft D3D12 Agility SDK package among the newest 41 holds the project's files"). The DLL's hash now comes first, and the launcher finds Microsoft's 1.614.1. Update or rebuild from fork main and press Fix and verify again.

FSR 3 frame generation with DLSS off: the game closed a few seconds in

With FSR 3 frame generation on and DLSS upscaling off, the game stopped at a breakpoint in its own upscaler 5 to 11 seconds after the start (issues #272, #308, #331). FSR 3 frame generation now stays off unless DLSS upscaling is on, and the F1 menu says why: FRAME GEN OFF: FSR 3 NEEDS DLSS UPSCALING ON. Turn DLSS on (F1 > DLSS) to use it. Cards without DLSS start without frame generation instead of closing.

Windows 10: the game closed a second after it started

v2026.11.27.6 fixed the 0x887E0003 start-up error, and players on Windows 11 confirmed it. On Windows 10 the game then got a little further and closed. Windows 10's own Direct3D 12 refuses a kind of root signature the game's translated shaders need: descriptor heaps indexed directly. Microsoft's newer runtime (the D3D12 Agility SDK 1.614) takes them.

v2026.11.27.6 offered that download only when the shader model was too old. With an up-to-date driver, Windows 10 reports 6.8, so it never offered it. Now, on Windows 10 without a D3D12 folder, victory.exe always offers it at the first start:

  • Answer Y. It's Microsoft's own, from nuget.org, about 22 MB, once, signed by Microsoft.
  • Or download it by hand: run victory.exe get-d3d12 in that folder.

If you answered N or the download failed, the game still starts, with a warning.

releases.title: v2026.11.27.6: the D3D12 start-up fix (0x887E0003), working this time
releases.summary:
Fixes the 0x887E0003 start-up crash that v2026.11.27.4 and .5 were meant to fix and didn't ("D3D12SerializeVersionedRootSignature ... The D3D12 SDK version configuration of the host exe is invalid"). Put victory.exe beside game_scarlett_master.exe and double-click it, as before.

What was wrong

victory.exe tells Windows which Direct3D 12 version it wants. Windows read that number before the exe's own code could set it, so every start asked for 1.614. That fails:

  • on Windows 10 and on Windows 11 22H2/23H2 when there is no D3D12 folder beside victory.exe, and
  • when a repack or another guide put a 1.618 or 1.620 D3D12 folder there.

The fix

Direct3D 12 is now loaded only when it is first used, after the exe has picked the version:

  • With a D3D12 folder, it asks for that folder's version, whatever it is.
  • Without one, it asks for the version Windows already has (at most 1.614).

On Windows 10, whose own Direct3D 12 is too old for the game's shaders, it then offers to fetch 1.614 from Microsoft as intended (victory.exe get-d3d12 does it by hand).

No other changes from v2026.11.27.5.

releases.title: v2026.11.27.4: crash fixes
releases.summary:
Fixes for the crashes most of you reported today. Put victory.exe beside game_scarlett_master.exe and double-click it, as before.

Crash fixes

  • "D3D12 XDXR Error: Failed to allocate upload buffer" after the loading screen (most often with DLSS on; RTX 4090, 5080, 5090 and others). By the first ray-traced frame, the address range the game's ray tracing needs was already full on some PCs. The exe now reserves that range the moment it starts. If it ever runs out anyway, it carries on instead of crashing, and it no longer retries thousands of times a frame (PR #88 found that half of it independently).
  • 0x887E0003, "The D3D12 SDK version configuration of the host exe is invalid" right at the start. This happened when a D3D12 folder from a repack or another guide (D3D12Core.dll 1.618 or 1.620) sat beside victory.exe. The exe now reads that file's version and uses it, so any 1.6xx runtime there works.
  • Memory that kept growing until the PC ran out (late-session slowdowns, "not enough memory" errors, coloured squares on faces): PR #58. The same view no longer becomes a new table entry each time the game rewrites its padding, and entries no resource owns are capped at a million.

Also

  • Phone calls, TVs and reverb are heard (PR #77): the game's audio convolutions are now computed. VICTORY_DSP_CONVOLVE=0 turns this off.
  • C: drive full? Run setx VICTORY_HOME D:\victory once, then start victory.exe from a new window. Settings, saves, caches, logs and downloads all go there instead of %LOCALAPPDATA%\victory. Move that folder's contents over first to keep what you have.

Still not supported: GTX 10- and 16-series cards (no mesh shaders).

releases.title: VIctory on NVIDIA 2026-11-27 (3): MFG Unlocker option
releases.summary:
One file, nothing to build. New since the previous release (2026-11-27 (2)): MFG Unlocker is now an option in the F1 menu. That mod lets RTX 20 and 30 cards try DLSS frame generation. Turn it on and the game downloads and loads it by itself. Everything else is as in 2026-11-27 (2): Windows 10 support, the F1 preload fix, the one-time warm-up and AMD's FSR 3 files.

How to use it

  1. Download victory.exe below.
  2. Put it into the folder of your own dump of the title's Xbox Series build v1.0.2.1, next to game_scarlett_master.exe.
  3. Double-click it. Windows may say the publisher is unknown (the file is not signed): "More info", then "Run anyway".

The first start of this version restarts the game by itself once. It plays about 20 seconds, says so at the top of the picture, then closes and opens again. This happens once per new version. Without it, a new version's first start stays at about 14 fps.

The first start also asks once whether to download NVIDIA's DLSS and frame generation files (about 70 MB, from NVIDIA's own GitHub). On a card without DLSS frame generation it also offers AMD's FSR 3 files (about 30 MB, from AMD's own GitHub). They belong to NVIDIA and AMD and are not part of this program. If you say no, the game still runs without them. victory.exe get-dlss and victory.exe get-fsr fetch them later.

In the game: F1 is the settings menu, F3 the stats panel.

MFG Unlocker (RTX 20 and 30): new

MFG Unlocker is someone else's mod (MIT licence). It unlocks DLSS frame generation on GeForce RTX 20 and 30 cards. NVIDIA does not support that, and the mod was not tested with this game: this fork is tested on an RTX 50.

  • To turn it on: F1, MFG UNLOCKER (MOD, RTX 20/30), ON, then restart.
  • What the next start does: it downloads the mod's v1.7.2 release from the mod's own GitHub (about 5 MB) into %LOCALAPPDATA%\victory\mfg-unlocker. It checks the zip and MFGUnlocker.dll against the SHA-256 hashes the mod's author published, and keeps nothing that doesn't match.
  • Loading: victory.exe loads the mod at every start, before NVIDIA's frame generation. You don't rename or copy anything.
  • First start on an RTX 20 or 30 card: the game asks once whether to turn it on. It stays off unless you type y.
  • victory.exe get-mfg downloads it by hand.
  • In the game: the start notice says "UNLOCKED BY A MOD" and Backspace opens the mod's own menu. The mod writes its own RTXMFG-... logs and settings next to victory.exe.
  • If the game crashes or frame generation fails: turn it off in F1. If the game doesn't get that far, add the line VICTORY_MFG_UNLOCKER= to %LOCALAPPDATA%\victory\victory-settings.txt.
  • The old way still works too: the mod renamed to winmm.dll and put next to victory.exe.

What was tested here: the loading at start, with a harmless Windows DLL in the mod's place. It loads before NVIDIA's frame generation starts, and the game runs normally. The download and the mod itself were not tested here.

Frame generation: what your card supports

Your card Frame generation Limits
GeForce RTX 40 and RTX 50 DLSS frame generation 2x on RTX 40; up to 6x on RTX 50
GeForce RTX 20 and RTX 30 AMD FSR 3 frame generation, or DLSS frame generation with MFG Unlocker (above) FSR 3: 2x at most. DLSS upscaling still works, so the Series X profile is fine
Other cards (no DLSS) AMD FSR 3 frame generation 2x at most, Series S profile only (F1, CONSOLE). Not tested

Windows 10

Windows 10's own Direct3D 12 can't run the shaders this layer makes: it stops at shader model 6.5, and they need 6.6. On a PC like that, the first start explains this and offers Microsoft's newer Direct3D 12 runtime. That is D3D12Core.dll from Microsoft's own package on nuget.org, about 22 MB, downloaded once. It goes into a D3D12 folder next to victory.exe. victory.exe get-d3d12 does the same by hand. Windows 11 keeps using its own runtime and downloads nothing. This was tested with Microsoft's runtime loaded from the D3D12 folder, but not on a Windows 10 PC.

Reporting a problem

Please attach both logs from the run that went wrong:

  1. The play log: the newest victory-nvidia-play-<date>-<time>-<number>.log in %LOCALAPPDATA%\victory\logs\. The console shows its path at the start.
  2. The crash log: %LOCALAPPDATA%\VIctory\data\7952987A\crashes.log, plus the newest victory-<date>-<time>-<number>.crash.log in %LOCALAPPDATA%\VIctory\data\7952987A\temp\ if there is one.

Also say which GPU, Windows version (10 or 11) and release you used, and whether MFG Unlocker was on.

What you need

  • Windows 10 or 11 (x64), 32 GB of RAM or more, an SSD.
  • A GeForce RTX card with a recent driver (tested on RTX 40 and RTX 50). Other cards are not tested.
  • Your own dump of the title. This release contains no game files, NVIDIA files, AMD files, Microsoft runtime or mod.

Good to know

  • Settings, saves, caches, logs, NVIDIA's and AMD's files and MFG Unlocker are kept under %LOCALAPPDATA%\victory. Two things can end up next to victory.exe: the D3D12 folder (only on a PC that needs it, like Windows 10), and MFG Unlocker's own logs and settings when the mod is on.
  • The first minutes of a first run stutter while shaders are translated and the driver compiles them. Run PRELOAD SHADERS first to avoid that; later runs are smooth.
  • About 25-28 frames a second on an RTX 5070 at 2560x1440 with DLSS Quality, before frame generation.
  • victory.exe play --help lists the options.

The file

  • victory.exe, built from commit 0cef07e of this repository with cargo build --release --locked -p victory and the C runtime linked in (-C target-feature=+crt-static).

releases.summary:
One file, nothing to build. New since 2026-11-26: AMD FSR 3 frame generation for cards without DLSS frame generation, a start notice saying what your card supports, shader preloading from the F1 menu, PS5 controllers, and a set of picture and stability fixes.

How to use it

  1. Download victory.exe below.
  2. Put it into the folder of your own dump of the title's Xbox Series build v1.0.2.1, next to game_scarlett_master.exe.
  3. Double-click it. Windows may say the publisher is unknown (the file is not signed): "More info", then "Run anyway".

The first start asks once whether to download NVIDIA's DLSS and frame generation files (about 70 MB) from NVIDIA's own GitHub. They are NVIDIA's and are not part of this program; say no and the game still runs, with its own upscaling and no DLSS. victory.exe get-dlss fetches them later.

In the game: F1 is the settings menu, F3 the stats panel.

Frame generation: what your card supports

Your card Frame generation Limits
GeForce RTX 40 and RTX 50 DLSS frame generation 2x on RTX 40; up to 6x on RTX 50
GeForce RTX 20 and RTX 30 AMD FSR 3 frame generation 2x at most; DLSS upscaling still works, so the Series X profile is fine
Other cards (no DLSS) AMD FSR 3 frame generation 2x at most, Series S profile only (F1, CONSOLE). Not tested
  • At every start the game says which one runs on your card, and why not if it can't, at the top of the picture for 30 seconds and in the console window.
  • F1, FRAME GEN TYPE: AUTO (DLSS where the card has it, else FSR 3), DLSS, or FSR 3.
  • FSR 3 needs AMD's FidelityFX DLLs, amd_fidelityfx_loader_dx12.dll and amd_fidelityfx_framegeneration_dx12.dll, from AMD's FidelityFX SDK (2.x). They are AMD's and not part of this release: put them in a folder named fidelityfx next to victory.exe.

  • AMD FSR 3 frame generation (2x), with the picture without the HUD handed to it, so the HUD and subtitles do not double or smear when you move.
  • Start notice: your GPU, which frame generation runs, and what to change if it is off (DLSS turned off, NVIDIA files not found, or a card without DLSS).

  • About 26-30 frames a second on an RTX 5070 at 2560x1440 with DLSS Quality, before frame generation.
